name: Singapore
note: Mental Capacity Act 2008, Probate and Administration Act 1934 and Human Organ Transplant Act 1987, from Singapore Statutes Online. The lasting power of attorney follows the England and Wales model but is stricter at the front: the Act says the power is not created at all unless the instrument is made and registered. Organ donation runs the other way from most of this set — consent is presumed and a registered objection is what blocks removal. Advance medical directives and disposal of remains sit in other statutes not retrieved for this entry.

roles.name: Donee of a lasting power of attorney (property and affairs)
roles.summary: Registration is constitutive, not administrative: the Act says a lasting power of attorney is not created unless the instrument is made and registered in accordance with the First Schedule. Authority then covers property and affairs, and operates when P no longer has capacity to decide.

assigned.event: P executes an instrument conferring authority over property and affairs on a donee who meets the statutory requirements

starts.event: The power is not created until the instrument is made and registered; the authority then operates when P no longer has capacity to make the decision

ends.event: P revokes the power at any time while having capacity to do so
Death of P; the estate passes to the personal representative

states.label: Made and registered; not yet operative
Donee acting for P over property and affairs

transitions.event: Instrument executed and registered in accordance with the First Schedule; without that the power is not created (s 11(2))
P no longer has capacity to make the decision (s 11(1))
P revokes while having capacity (s 15(2))
Death of P; probate or administration follows (Probate and Administration Act s 8)

roles.name: Donee of a lasting power of attorney (personal welfare)
roles.summary: The same instrument may confer authority over personal welfare, and it works the same way: created only on registration, exercisable only once P lacks capacity for the decision in question.

assigned.event: P executes an instrument conferring authority over personal welfare on a donee who meets the statutory requirements

starts.event: On registration, and when P no longer has capacity to make the welfare decision

ends.event: P revokes the power at any time while having capacity to do so
Death of P; the estate passes to the personal representative

states.label: Made and registered; not yet operative
Donee deciding personal welfare for P

transitions.event: Instrument executed and registered; the power is not created otherwise (s 11(2))
P no longer has capacity for the welfare decision (s 11(1)(a))
P revokes while having capacity (s 15(2))
Death of P (Probate and Administration Act s 8)

roles.name: Deputy for property and affairs
roles.summary: Where P lacks capacity the court may either make the decision itself or appoint a deputy to make it. A deputy over property and affairs must be 21 or over and act without remuneration, unless they are a professional deputy unrelated to P.

assigned.event: Court finds P lacks capacity in relation to property and affairs and appoints a deputy rather than deciding the matter itself

starts.event: On appointment, within the powers the order confers

ends.event: Death of P; the estate passes to the personal representative

states.label: Deputy acting under the court order

transitions.event: Court appoints a deputy for property and affairs (ss 20, 24)
Death of P (Probate and Administration Act s 8)

roles.name: Deputy for personal welfare
roles.summary: The same power lets the court appoint a deputy for personal welfare. The Act frames appointment as the alternative to the court deciding the matter itself, so the deputy exists only to the extent the order says.

assigned.event: Court finds P lacks capacity in relation to personal welfare and appoints a deputy rather than deciding the matter itself

starts.event: On appointment, within the powers the order confers

states.label: Deputy acting under the court order

transitions.event: Court appoints a deputy for personal welfare (ss 20, 24)
Death of P (Probate and Administration Act s 8)

roles.name: Executor
roles.summary: Probate may be granted to any executor appointed by a will, and the appointment may be express or implied. Where a will appoints several, probate may issue to one or more without prejudice to a later grant to the others.

assigned.event: Will appoints an executor, expressly or by implication

starts.event: On the grant of probate; where several are appointed, probate may be granted to one or more of them

states.label: Appointed by the will, expressly or impliedly

transitions.event: Will appoints an executor, expressly or by implication (s 8(1)-(2))
Probate granted; where several are appointed it may issue to one or more (s 8(3))
Administration of the estate completed (s 8)

roles.name: Administrator
roles.summary: On intestacy the court may grant letters of administration, having regard to the rights of everyone interested in the estate. Where security is required it is ordinarily a bond by the grantee and two sureties in the sworn amount of the estate.

assigned.event: Person dies intestate and the court considers the rights of all persons interested in the estate

starts.event: On the grant of letters of administration, subject to any security the registrar requires

states.label: Security required; bond by grantee and two sureties

transitions.event: Registrar determines the sufficiency of security; ordinarily a bond with two sureties in the sworn amount (s 29)
Court grants letters of administration on intestacy, having regard to all interested persons (s 18)
Grant made where no security is required (ss 18, 29(3))
Administration of the estate completed (s 18)

roles.name: Designated officer authorising organ removal, subject to a registered objection
roles.summary: Singapore presumes consent. A hospital’s designated officer may authorise removal of an organ from a person who died there, and the block is not a missing consent but a registered objection: no authority may be given where the deceased registered an objection with the Director-General during their lifetime. An objection may be withdrawn at any time.

assigned.event: A person may register an objection to removal of an organ with the Director-General, in the prescribed form, or leave the register untouched

starts.event: On death in hospital the designated officer may authorise removal in writing, unless the deceased had registered an objection

ends.event: Removal authorised and carried out, or barred by a registered objection

transitions.event: Person registers an objection with the Director-General, entered on a register not open to public inspection (ss 8, 9)
Objection withdrawn in the prescribed form and removed from the register (s 10)
Death in hospital; the designated officer authorises removal in writing (s 4(1))
Death in hospital, but no authority may be given because an objection was registered in the deceased’s lifetime (s 4(2)(a))

poaRegistrationBeforeUse.note: A lasting power of attorney is not created unless the instrument is made and registered in accordance with the First Schedule, so registration is constitutive rather than a later formality.

healthAgentStartsOn.note: The donee’s authority is over decisions P can no longer make; the instrument confers it for when P no longer has capacity.

organDonationModel.note: The designated officer may authorise removal after death in hospital, and no authority may be given only where the deceased registered an objection with the Director-General in their lifetime. Objections may be withdrawn.
